name: New User: Signup to First Design
description: Complete journey from landing page visit through account creation to first design completion
primary_user_goal: Create a professional-looking design without prior design experience
business_goal: Convert visitor to registered user with completed first design (activation)
entry_point: Landing page or template gallery (via search/referral)
friction_points: Template decision paralysis (mitigated by smart recommendations)
Learning editor interface (reduced by intuitive design and tips)
notes: This flow is Canva's core activation funnel. The genius is that users often start editing BEFORE completing signup - they select a template, make a few edits, then are prompted to sign up to save. This demonstrates value before asking for commitment.

name: Template to Finished Design
description: Core creation flow from template selection through customization to export
primary_user_goal: Transform a template into a personalized, share-ready design
business_goal: Deliver value that drives return usage and word-of-mouth
friction_points: Finding the right template (solved by smart search and categories)
Customizing without breaking design (solved by smart layouts)
Exporting in correct format (solved by smart defaults)
notes: This is the core product loop. Key insight: templates do 80% of the design work, user does 20% customization but feels 100% ownership. The flow is optimized to minimize time-to-value while maximizing perceived creativity.

name: Returning User: Continue or Create
description: Returning user journey to resume work or start new project
primary_user_goal: Quickly access previous work or start new design efficiently
business_goal: Maintain engagement habit and deepen platform investment
entry_point: Login or direct link to home
friction_points: Finding previous work (solved by recent designs and search)
Remembering where to find features (solved by consistent UI)
Decision fatigue for new designs (solved by quick-create buttons)
notes: Returning users are Canva's most valuable segment. The home dashboard is optimized for continuation - recent work is immediately visible. The goal is to get users into the editor as fast as possible, whether resuming or starting fresh.

name: Free to Pro Upgrade
description: Conversion journey from free user to paid subscriber
primary_user_goal: Access premium features to improve design capabilities
business_goal: Convert free users to paying subscribers
entry_point: Various upgrade touchpoints (premium content, feature limit, pricing page)
friction_points: Uncertainty about Pro value (solved by feature previews)
Commitment anxiety (solved by monthly option and cancel anytime)
conversion_triggers: Hitting usage limits on AI features
notes: Canva's upgrade flow is remarkably non-pushy. Premium features are visible and desirable but don't block core workflows. The 30-day free trial is the primary conversion mechanism - it removes purchase risk and creates commitment through usage.

name: AI/Magic Tools Discovery and Usage
description: User journey discovering and using Canva's AI-powered features
primary_user_goal: Leverage AI to create or enhance designs faster
business_goal: Differentiate through AI capabilities; drive Pro upgrades for unlimited AI
entry_point: Magic Studio hub or contextual AI suggestions in editor
friction_points: Understanding AI capabilities (solved by clear examples)
AI quality concerns (solved by iteration options)
Usage limits on free tier (soft friction driving upgrades)
ai_features: Magic Design - Generate designs from prompts
Magic Eraser - Remove objects from images
Text to Image - Generate images from prompts
success_metrics: Pro upgrades from AI limit hits
notes: AI features are strategically integrated throughout Canva rather than siloed. The 'Magic' branding makes AI approachable. Free tier includes limited AI uses, creating natural upgrade moments without hard blocks. Quality of AI output is tuned for design context, not generic generation.

name: Team Collaboration Flow
primary_user_goal: Collaborate with team members on designs efficiently
business_goal: Drive Teams tier adoption through collaboration value
entry_point: Share button or direct invite link
friction_points: Understanding who changed what (solved by version history)
Conflicting simultaneous edits (solved by real-time sync)
notes: Collaboration is a key driver for Teams tier adoption. Real-time multiplayer editing (Google Docs-style) is smooth and responsive. The sharing model is flexible - view, comment, or edit permissions. Brand Kit sharing ensures enterprise consistency across team designs.
